thread:
anna-m: quick sanity check — i'm trying to land an autotune flow for SLO thresholds surfaced in the console. current derivation idea: per-tenant threshold = p95_baseline + alpha * rolling_std(p95, 24h). goal is to adapt to baseline drift but avoid chasing spikes and blowing up notify fanout. any obvious flaws? :thinking:

kevin-r: sounds reasonable as a start. couple concerns: 1) small-sample tenants will have unstable stddevs, 2) aggressive alpha can enlarge thresholds and hide regressions, 3) notify fanout might still spike if many tenants update thresholds simultaneously.

lee: agree with kevin. suggest adding a min_samples check and a max_delta cap. also consider EWMA for the baseline rather than raw p95 window — it smooths transient spikes. hysteresis is important: only roll forward/back after N consecutive windows.

anna-m: good call. thinking config knobs: min_samples (default 100), max_delta_pct (default 25%), alpha (default 1.5), hysteresis_windows (default 3). can we sketch a compact config snippet?

kevin-r: yep. also add a "notify_weight_bias" field so threshold changes don't immediately change notify fanout weight. separate derivation from routing policy. that gives ops time to observe.

anna-m: draft config i had in mind:

```yaml
autotune:
  metric: p95_latency_ms
  baseline_window: 24h
  alpha: 1.5
  min_samples: 100
  max_delta_pct: 25
  hysteresis_windows: 3
  ewma_alpha: 0.2
  notify_weight_bias: 0.5 # 0=no bias(direct), 1=fully ignore autotune for routing
```

lee: nit: use absolute cap for max_delta too (e.g. 200ms) so tiny-baseline tenants don't get large relative changes. and document the failure mode when samples < min_samples (fall back to org-level default).

kevin-r: telemetry question — we need a synthetic signal to validate this before rolling. propose a canary cohort (5% tenants) and a shadow run that computes proposed thresholds and triggers no-notify alerts, then compare alert counts and percentiles week-over-week.

slo-bot: autotune-sanitycheck started for canary cohort id=autotune-canary-2026-03. running shadow comparison job (3h window).

anna-m: perfect. we'll do shadow for 72h, then a short canary where notify_weight_bias=0.8 so routing changes are throttled. if alert volume delta < 5% and regression rate low, we can widen.

kevin-r: remember rate-limit backpressure on notify service — add a soft-rate cap so if notify QB > X we throttle new derived thresholds.

lee: i'll add EWMA implementation and the hysteresis logic to the derivation lib, plus unit tests for edgecases (nan stddev, constant series).

deploy-bot: FYI: scheduled the shadow job for 1724322000 and canary rollout window 1724400000-1724410000.

anna-m: thanks all — i'll update the RFC with the knobs and the rollout plan + telemetry dashboards to track derived_thresholds, notify_fanout_delta, canary_alert_delta. tagging @kevin-r @lee for review. :thumbsup:

kevin-r: +1

lee: +1, looking at the RFC after lunch.
